decoder_context: Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ is the full group of real n by n matrices with transpose(A) A = identity, with matrix multiplication, the inherited finite real matrix topology and its Borel sigma-algebra. The dimension can be zero, when the group is a singleton.

The displayed group is compact, nonempty, Hausdorff and second countable, with these facts constructed internally rather than caller premises. PositiveCompacts consists of compact sets with nonempty interior; top is the entire compact group.

Measure.haarMeasure K is the actual Haar construction normalized by assigning the positive compact set K mass one. IsHaarMeasure means left invariance, finiteness on compact sets and positivity on nonempty open sets. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one. Measure.map is pushforward.

Private-provider/proof audit of the whole module: Matrix.orthogonalGroup is the unitary subgroup over the trivial real star; Mathlib LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean:293-302 equates membership with transpose inverse, including the source's A^T A=I formulation for square finite matrices. No special-orthogonal/determinant-one restriction is present. The private measurableSpace is exactly borel of this subtype, and the BorelSpace witness is rfl, so there is no arbitrary sigma-algebra or discrete topology. Matrix topology is the ordinary function/product topology (Topology/Instances/Matrix.lean:48-52), and the subtype topology is inherited. The second-countability instance is obtained from finite products of R through Subtype.val; it is a proof of the actual topology's property, not a caller assumption.

Compactness is actually discharged: entry_norm_bound_of_unitary (Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Matrix.lean:49-50) bounds every entry by 1; Real.norm_eq_abs and abs_le convert this to entry membership in [-1,1]. Topology/Algebra/Star/Unitary.lean:31-36 makes the unitary set closed using continuous star and multiplication in the ambient matrix topology. IsCompact.matrix (Topology/Instances/Matrix.lean:68-70), isCompact_Icc, and closed-subset compactness prove this subtype compact. The group identity gives nonemptiness for every n. Hence PositiveCompacts.top is legitimately the entire group with nonempty interior (Topology/Sets/Compacts.lean:692-706). At n=0 the empty matrix type is a singleton; all entry-bound obligations are vacuous and the identity remains present. Nothing asserts two determinant components in dimension zero.

The measure is the actual normalized Mathlib construction, not an abstract parameter or a definition selected from the desired conclusion. Haar/Basic.lean:521-522 defines haarMeasure K0 by scaling Haar content; its self-normalization theorem at 542-548 gives mass 1 on K0, and the actual IsHaarMeasure instance at 574-579 provides left invariance, finiteness on compact sets, and positivity on nonempty open sets. The pinned uniqueness API actually proves the probability case via compactness; the lesson's mention of the second-countable group is true, although second countability is not an extra premise of that API. The constructor definition repeats this exact construction. The characterization separately proves its probability/Haar fields and genuinely applies existsUnique_orthogonalHaar.unique to the competitor and constructed measure. The last theorem installs this concrete Haar instance and invokes Group/Measure.lean:48-50, which is an equality of pushforward measures under left multiplication, not merely a total-mass identity. Left multiplication is continuous and Borel on this topological group. import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Matrix
import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Star.Unitary
import Mathlib.Topology.Instances.Matrix
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Real
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Unique
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.Integral

/-!
# Canonical Haar probability on the full real orthogonal group

Shared background for the two different experiments in Zhou--Suzuki,
arXiv:2610.20492v1: Section 2 / Appendix B.2.1 and Section 4.1.
Only the full Haar probability is common. Determinant conditioning, adaptive
posteriors, independence from an algorithm's seed and Krylov representations
are separate obligations. The construction includes dimension zero, without
asserting two determinant components in that dimension.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar

private instance orthogonal_measurableSpace (n : ℕ) :
    MeasurableSpace (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) := borel _

private instance orthogonal_borelSpace (n : ℕ) :
    BorelSpace (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) := ⟨rfl⟩

private instance orthogonal_secondCountable (n : ℕ) :
    SecondCountableTopology (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) := by
  let : SecondCountableTopology (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :=
    inferInstanceAs (SecondCountableTopology (Fin n → Fin n → ℝ))
  exact secondCountableTopology_induced (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)
    (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) Subtype.val

private instance orthogonal_compactSpace (n : ℕ) :
    CompactSpace (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) := by
  apply isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp
  apply (isCompact_Icc : IsCompact (Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1)).matrix.of_isClosed_subset
    (isClosed_unitary : IsClosed
      (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)))
  intro A hA
  change ∀ i j, A i j ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1
  intro i j
  exact abs_le.mp (by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using
    entry_norm_bound_of_unitary hA i j)

/-- Real well-definedness: there exists exactly one Borel Haar probability law. -/
theorem existsUnique_orthogonalHaar (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! μ : Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
      IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ μ.IsHaarMeasure := by
  let μ : Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :=
    Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := ⟨by
    simpa only [μ, PositiveCompacts.coe_top] using
      (Measure.haarMeasure_self (K₀ :=
        (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))))⟩
  have hhaar : μ.IsHaarMeasure := by dsimp only [μ]; infer_instance
  refine ⟨μ, ⟨hprob, hhaar⟩, ?_⟩
  intro ν hν
  let := hprob
  let := hhaar
  let := hν.1
  let := hν.2
  exact Measure.isHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure ν μ

/-- The actual Haar constructor normalized on the entire compact orthogonal group.
The preceding existence/uniqueness proof was independently audited before this definition. -/
noncomputable def orthogonalHaar (n : ℕ) :
    Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :=
  Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))

/-- Characterization and uniqueness of the constructed full Haar probability. -/
theorem orthogonalHaar_spec (n : ℕ) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (orthogonalHaar n) ∧ (orthogonalHaar n).IsHaarMeasure ∧
      ∀ μ : Measure (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
        IsProbabilityMeasure μ → μ.IsHaarMeasure → μ = orthogonalHaar n := by
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure (orthogonalHaar n) := ⟨by
    simpa only [orthogonalHaar, PositiveCompacts.coe_top] using
      (Measure.haarMeasure_self (K₀ :=
        (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))))⟩
  have hhaar : (orthogonalHaar n).IsHaarMeasure := by
    dsimp only [orthogonalHaar]
    infer_instance
  refine ⟨hprob, hhaar, ?_⟩
  intro μ hp hh
  exact (existsUnique_orthogonalHaar n).unique ⟨hp, hh⟩ ⟨hprob, hhaar⟩

/-- The source's full Haar draw has the same law after every fixed left rotation/reflection. -/
theorem orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left (n : ℕ)
    (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => Q * O) = orthogonalHaar n := by
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).2.1
  exact map_mul_left_eq_self (orthogonalHaar n) Q

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar

reconstruction.text: Define a family of Borel measures rho_n on the full real orthogonal groups O(n), for every natural number n including zero, by rho_n := Measure.haarMeasure(top : PositiveCompacts(O(n))). Here O(n) = {A in R^(n x n) : A^T A = I} has the inherited finite real matrix topology and its Borel sigma-algebra, top is the entire compact group, and the actual Haar construction is normalized to assign that entire group mass one. This displayed expression is a definition of a measure-valued function of n, rather than a separate theorem asserting uniqueness.
